Peripheral vascular disease The term peripheral vascular disease is often used for atherosclerotic or occlusive arterial disease but in its wid- est sense covers both arterial and venous disorders and may be due to atherosclerosis, vasospasm, or thromboem- bolism. Peripheral arterial occlusive disorders are the sub- ject of the following discussion; for reviews of vasospastic arterial disorders see p.1188. Venous disorders are covered under Venous Thromboembolism (p.1189); for chronic venous disease see also Varicose Veins (p.2347) and Wounds and Ulcers (p.1585). The commonest form of occlusive arterial disease is caused by atherosclerosis.
